verdict.tagline: Divine action and deep progression, tempered by heavy late-game grinding.
for_you_if: you loved the frantic combat and deep progression of the original
you want smooth action backed by top-tier music and art
you enjoy experimenting with diverse builds and weapon aspects
not_for_you_if: you dislike extensive resource grinding and material gathering
you want quick and direct story progression without random bottlenecks
you prefer fast movement mechanics right from the start

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the protagonist's movement, including the dash and sprint mechanics, feels slower and less responsive compared to the first game.

citations.review_text:
Harika oyun diyerek başlamak istiyorum lafa, ilkine göre yapılacak ve denenecek tonla şey var.
Karakter tasarımları, konsept, kurgu yine yerli yerinde. Seslendirmeleri sevdim, şarkılarına bayıldım. 

Erken erişimden çıkmasını bekledim uzun bir zaman nihayetinde vakit bulduğum zaman deneyeyim dedim fakat beni çok şaşırttı.
Witch temalı bir şablonda oynayacağımızın farkındaydım da silah seçeneklerinin bu kadar kötü olmasını beklemiyordum. Witch staff ve gocaman baltamız dışında zerre zevk alamadım, kaldı ki onlar da bir çeşit "menzile" sahip. İşin daha da kötü kısmı, menzilini belli eden bir ibre bulunmamakta. 
İlk oyun kadar hızlı değil, klavye kontrollerinden nefret ettim. Kolla oynamak da zevk vermedi. 
Neden *Sprint* diye bir şey getirmişler, inanın çözemedim. Karakterimizin kontrolü ilk oyunki kadar rahat gelmedi bana, akamıyorum patır kütür. Düşmanlar fazla yavaş, oyun benden kapışmamış değil, menzil tutmamı bekliyor.
Zagreus ile oynarken mızrak/kalkan/yumruk odaklı oynuyordum daha çok, belki benim zevkime uymamıştır Hades 2. 

Yine de seveni için üstüne çıkılmış, daha nitelikli bir oyun inşa edildiği açık. Keşke sevebilseydim, belki de bitirmeyi denerim.

Not Recommended
If you loved the first Hades for its frantic pace, aggressive dash-heavy gameplay, and clear, fair combat rules—skip this one. The sequel feels like tedious math and a total disappointment.
I honestly tried to adapt and play differently, but it’s just not fun. The game suffocates and punishes you at every turn:

Controls and Dynamics
Forget Zagreus’s sharp, spammable dashes. Melinoë feels sluggish, and her dash is heavy with a noticeable delay. Instead of cleanly dodging through attacks, you are forced to hold down sprint and tediously run in circles away from enemies.

Spongy Mobs and Armor
Enemies are just bloated with HP. Because of the overtuned armor, you rush in, unleash a combo, and the mob completely ignores your hits—they just strike right through your attacks.

Visual Clutter and Unreadability
The floor is always littered with garbage: tons of AOE circles, puddles, particle effects, and completely unreadable homing projectiles flying from god knows where. You constantly take tons of cheap damage here.

Clunky Arena Design
The developers built the gameplay around running, yet they cluttered the arenas with rocks, fences, and terrain debris that block your movement. You literally trip over the geometry mid-fight while a bullet hell is flying straight at you.

Instead of high-octane action, we got a waiting simulator packed with annoying mechanics. And that's not even mentioning the bland story, a hollow protagonist, and a mountain of weird resources with a mobile-game-tier grind.

Combat just feels so much slower than in the first game, I just can't put my finger on exactly what else it is that makes me disappointed in this game. If there was an option, I'd put "mixed feelings", but overall I just can't recommend this game when it doesn't stack up compared to the original in my eyes.
Will probably revisit this game later

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game runs smoothly and is well optimized, including on a Mac or Steam deck.

citations.review_text: Very fun gameplay loop, albeit the game can kind of confusing if you didn't play the first game. (An easy way to solve that problem is by just playing the first game tbh because its also AMAZING) This series contains some of if not THE best action rougelikes on the market and they DID NOT miss with this sequel. The story writing is engaging throughout all of you runs; I don't think that I've honestly heard the same piece of dialogue twice. This game is definitely worth its weight in gold for all that it provides and could basically runs like butter on a potato when it comes to optimization. BUY THE GAME ALREADY!

I played Hades on my PS4, and ever since then I’ve been itching to play Hades II, which isn’t available on the PS4. I was trying to figure out how to get my hands on a PS5, but with the stock shortages in India, I ended up here on Steam instead.

This was my first time trying Steam on a Mac, and I’m glad it worked out. The game is an absolute blast. Supergiant has done it again!

If you enjoyed the first one, you'll love this - it feels like they dialed everything about the original to 11. Also, the game is ridiculously well optimized. I'm running 4k, 120fps, no frame drops - and my GPU hotspot stays under 70.
i think this game solves a lot of the issues that the first game had and i really enjoy it on steam deck

cohorts.summary: Mid-game players highlight the dual-route progression and varied builds, alongside heavy grinding and slow story pacing.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes dual-route progression with paths going both up toward the surface and down.

citations.review_text:
[h1] A SPELLBINDING SEQUEL THAT ELEVATES THE MYTH [/h1]

[b][i]  Following up on a masterpiece is no easy task, but this sequel proves that the flame of the Underworld burns brighter than ever. Stepping into the boots of Melinoë brings a completely fresh, witchcraft-infused combat style that feels distinct, tactical, and incredibly fluid compared to Zagreus.

The addition of Omega moves, the dual-route progression between Chronos and the surface, and an entirely new roster of gods and boons make the gameplay loop addictively deep. Even without uncovering every single secret yet, the rich storytelling, stunning art direction, and stellar soundtrack make it a flawless and worthy successor to its legendary predecessor.

Death to Chronos. 9.5/10  [/i][/b]

Takes the masterpiece of the first game and improves upon it in nearly every way. Swapping between surface and underground runs keeps the game feeling fresh and keeps any one side from feeling stale. The customization of weapons, companions, and boons lead to the player learning multiple playstyles and allows them to tweak things until they find powerful combos and synergies. I've finished the main story and yet I still feel that there's dozens of hours of contnet remaining, and a couple storylines still left to complete. This game is amazing, buy it, then go buy Hades and finish that THEN come play this one.

Game is amazing!
A lot of combinations to choose, i like that there are 2 paths now, up and down, gives a lot of deep to the story, and the story is amazing.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that story progression depends on random character encounters, which can make advancing specific questlines slow or tedious.

citations.review_text:
Very conflicted about this one. The gameplay, the music, the characters, the art, it's all absolutely stellar. But the story progression is painfully slow. Advancing some of the story only one interaction at a time per run, and it's still based on random encounters, and other text lines might take priority, it's just tedious. I'm well over 100 runs in, I've done almost all of the minor prophecies, but various questlines are barely halfway done, or haven't even triggered, despite talking to all characters at every opportunity.

I really enjoyed the first 40 hrs or so, after that I was just trying to wrap things up, and at this point I'll just stop. I triggered the true ending, and that's it. So, great game, lots of fun, but just be prepared that you're a slave to random encounters, and they may simply not trigger to advance every story line...

If you liked the first game then this game is probably going to be enjoyable to you too, unless, and this is sadly a big unless, that you are like me and do not like anyone in the main cast of this game...

My favourite character as of 50 hours into the game is a frog that does not even speak.

To clarify the characters are not poorly written or entirely unlikable, but they are just kinda boring, Skelly from the first game has a less personal relationship with Melinoe than he did with Zagreous and everyone else requires too much time to become interesting in their own right or just have the most acerbic personalities possible.

It also does not help that the story feels lackluster and lacking focus at times. 

Overall a good game, but not nearly as good of an experience as the first one was.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires significant grinding and gathering of multiple currencies and materials.

citations.review_text:
Hades 2 is just a worse Hades 1. Seeing as it's reviewed as Overwhelmingly Positive I'm gonna take it that Hades is just not a game franchise made for me (even though I liked the first one). Definitely not buying Hades 3 if that ever comes out.

Hades 2 has :
more mindless grinding....
more currencies and materials you need to gather...
more cringe dialogue...
worse combat...
worse storyline...
worse soundtrack...

Hades 2 bosses are alright; I liked Prometheus, Chronos and Typhon and absolutely despise the "Queens of Cringe" aka Scylla and Eris. The new weapons are "meh" and the new biomes (mostly) look great but that's about it. I think what I like the most about Hades 2 are the Chaos challenges; those are cool.

Great game, but I don't feel the same rush as I did when I played the first game. 
Maybe it's because I'm coming to Hades 2 right after finishing Hades 1. 
What I liked about Hades 1 was how nicely the game incentivized trying new things, keeping things fresh with what would otherwise be a repetitive gameplay. 
Since it's somewhat the same formula here, I couldn't find joy in that anymore.
Overall, I think there's more to grind in this game, and I can't find myself spending the time to get all the achievements.
I would still recommend if you liked Hades 1, has all the same great elements.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features smooth, responsive combat with a wide variety of builds and weapon aspects.

citations.review_text:
ꨄ My rating: 10/10 ꨄ

Pros:
- Everything that Hades did well, Hades 2 did even better. One of them was increasing the number of weapon aspects available and adding new creative ways of playing with them, making nearly all gods and weapon combinations at least viable.
- The story and artstyle isn't as heartwarming and colorful as the first game. Instead the sequel is a bit more gloomy. This time it features a big plot twist once you reach the "true ending" of the game, that will surely surprise people who aren't as familiar with Greek Mythology.
- The main character, Melinoë, despite not being as funny and charismatic as Zagreus, is still very iconic and features lots of funny moments in game due to her more serious personality.
- Essentially, if you enjoyed Hades, you will likely enjoy Hades 2 even more!

Cons: 
- There is genuinely nothing I can think of that can be perceived as negative in this game. One of the few games I dare to call perfect.

9/10 – Fast roguelike with a good story, better and bigger than the first.

Good:
- Smooth and responsive combat
- Great art and animations
- Good music
- Good story and characters
- A lot of build variety
- Lots of weapons 
- Every run feels different
- There is always progression to be made

Bad:
- Some weapons feel weaker
- Not as surprising if you played the first

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Rating to the follow-up game of Hades

Hades II somehow pulls off the impossible: it takes everything that made the first game amazing and makes it bigger, deeper, and even more addictive.

The combat feels faster and more strategic, the build variety is insane, and every run gives you another reason to say, "just one more." Melinoë is a fantastic protagonist, bringing a different energy from Zagreus while still fitting perfectly into the world. The art, music, voice acting, and character writing are all top-tier, which is exactly what you'd expect from Supergiant Games.

What impressed me most is how polished the game feels. Even during Early Access, it launched with an enormous amount of content and was already being praised as one of the strongest Early Access releases in recent memory. Steam reviews remain overwhelmingly positive, with players praising the expanded gameplay systems, bosses, and progression.

Is it harder than the first game? Definitely. Some encounters can feel brutal, and a few mechanics might frustrate you at first. But every victory feels earned, and experimenting with different builds never gets old.

If you loved Hades, buying Hades II is a no-brainer. If you've never played either game, congratulations—you've just found the next 100+ hours of your life.

Pros:

Incredible combat and build variety
Amazing soundtrack and voice acting
Gorgeous art style
Tons of replayability
"Just one more run" syndrome is stronger than ever

Cons:

Sleep schedule may be permanently destroyed
Chronos doesn't care about your feelings

10/10 — The gods cooked again. 🔥

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players praise the refined combat and presentation, while pointing out extensive grinding and disappointing narrative conclusions.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat mechanics, including weapons, aspects, and build variety, as an improvement over the first game.

citations.review_text: Hades 2 is without doubt one of the best ARPG's made to date. If it had a coop I would lose my beeeeeeeans. All systems are improved from the previous entry. The lore is amazing and the visual style is peak Super Giant. The OST is remarkable 10/10 buy it, love it, rub it all over.

Hades was my favorite game of all time and this one my most anticipated sequel ever. Even with such high expectations I still loved Hades 2. It's better at everything and bigger than Hades 1. They caught lightning in a bottle twice. Gameplay feels great, the progression is fair and the art just insane.

If you're even remotely interested in the game, buy it

An incredible upgrade over the first game in almost every aspect. The weapons feel much more diverse, the combat itself more interesting with the addition of Omega attacks and mana, the trinkets more fun and worth switching during a run. Only the lore after the "main" ending and the romantic interests (ironically not really interesting) are less fleshed out than the first game.

Great game. I started with Hades so I'll use this review to compare Hades II to the original.

Gameplay:
Hades II has an edge. The weapons and aspects are an improvement, the Arcana Card system is flexible, and the wide variety of boons make a for ton of fun and viable builds.
Hades II also has a more carefully thought out reward system. It's possible to progress further in Hades II without as much of the relentless grinding that's needed in Hades.

Story:
Hades was superior to Hades II in this regard. Zagreus is a substantially more intriguing character than Melinoë. The central story of Hades is more touching, with a far better conclusion. While Hades II offers a broader cast, many of the additional characters add little to the experience. The epilogue was particularly lackluster.

I only got into this Hades last year, so I don't have a ton of history with it. But I greatly enjoyed the first game, I spent 180+ hours enjoying the story, the gameplay and getting to know all the different characters and their stories, so much so that I felt sad when I decided my time with the game was over.

Now I've reached the same point with Hades 2 and there's both relief and sorrow for "finishing" the game. This sequel is as worth of being a sequel to an incredible game as you're going to get, I cannot stress this enough. There's a lot of discourse about this or that and how the first Hades is better, I diisagree with most of that, Hades 2 is simply different in many ways and it tells a different story, while the story of the first is more relateable I find that I enjoyed both almost as much I would say.

My favorite thing about Hades 2 is the combat which in my opinion is head and shoulders above Hades 1, here you can have so many builds and synergies between all the different boons that it still surprises me, often you won't even get a duo boon yet you still melt everything in your path when you find the right build. In Hades 1 you felt like a wet noodle if you didn't find the exact boons and the duo boon to go with them, often the rng didn't give a crap and you struggled with the bosses. Here they did a tremendous job balancing all the different boons and things you could do with them, I can't remember the last time I wore one of the god's keepsakes, they are utterly unnecessary. And to me that is the best and most fun aspect of this game. 

I enjoyed the characters so much, they are different, especially Meli, I found that getting to know them and learn more about them made them more fun and interesting, not to mention the voice acting alone made me want to listen to every single line of dialogue they had. SGG never disappoints when it comes to characters and story telling. I did miss a couple of bonds so I could complete my funko pop collection bu…

claims.claim: Reviewers express disappointment with the narrative ending and character story resolutions.

citations.review_text: i have my issues with the story's ending, but besides that it might be better than the first one in almost every way.

Gameplay is 10 out of 10.

Story ending is complete garbage imo.

Also, unskippable credits at the end that span for 7-8 minutes seems forced. Without sitting through already disappointing finale you have to endure a tedious credit scene or you are unable to progress and play the game. 

its an easy fix that the devs seems to have refused to put in just as a statement. Sadly a negative outcome to a otherwise positive game.

It's hard to say "not recommended" on a game that I've put 112 hours into. Early access was very fun and gameplay-wise I have little to complain about. It does many things better than the first Hades game, some worse, but is overall an improvement. If you only care for the gameplay, this game will surely be a blast, by all means, GLHF.

But I cannot stress how big of a letdown story-wise it has been.

Before launch, there were many things hinted at that would be expanded upon as the updates were being released. I was excited to learn what both the main story and the many interesting side quests had to offer, only to be thoroughly disappointed with almost every. single. one.

I was wondering how the main story was going to end, especially assuming the game would follow its predecessor in still allowing you to play after the ending. In my worst predictions, I could not have anticipated how rushed and badly written it actually turned out to be. It felt like a spit in the face and a waste of time spent on the game up until that point.

The vast majority of side quests also make you feel like you wasted your time on them. They might be really entertaining, or even exciting, to do, up until the last dialogue that makes it all just... not matter. Almost all of them end with the same thing: [spoiler] the character making you feel bad for trying to help [/spoiler].

The absolute worst example of this is [spoiler] waking up Hypnos [/spoiler]. Teased in I'm pretty sure every early access update since its first part, it seemed like something big was planned for it. There wasn't. It ends with [spoiler] a joke at the protag's expense and Hypnos just disappears forever. [/spoiler] Great. I love when developers make me feel excited and then purposefully don't deliver.

If you've been keeping on top of the quests until the epilogue, it leaves you wondering... what is the message of the game supposed to be? What's the moral of the story? [spoiler] That everybody can be redeemed (main…

Gameplay is fine. If you like roguelites then this is the king. 

But if you want a good story look elsewhere. The original ending was done so poorly that due to the backlash Supergiant had to come back to the drawing board to level out their franchise better. 

My complaint comes from the writing. This game has the most inferior writing compared to the original. 

Every side character has very little character arcs and Arachne is the worst offender to all of them. We spend multiple runs [spoiler] building up a story of how she has changed and ready to ask for her old body back. [/spoiler] 
Arachne was the only character I wanted to see change. And I'm supposed to believe [spoiler] the goddess of WISDOM is petulant enough to not let go of a grudge. Are you serious? [/spoiler]. I'd expect that kind of arrogance from Zeus and Hera.

I dropped this game for months after the original request for the [spoiler] "nothing beats the power of family!" [/spoiler] ending and wish I had never picked it back up. I only bought this game in early access because of the proven story of Hades 1 and I will not make the same mistake again if Supergiant is this afraid to make their characters have interesting arcs. Telling stories where a character just doubles down is bad writing. Then the game continues this bad writing with Echo who chooses to remain a statue in a place of suffering. Like WTF?? How many different ways can you tell the same freaking story. 

This game does not deserve the overwhelming positive reviews that it has.

Good game, sadly completed it all before they added more dialouge and I was too lazy to re do stuff.

I think out of the two games the first one has a better feel for fighting solely based on the fact U speed around with dodgeing around more so my ADHD brain feels like im doing more.

Some of the wepons and accesories are just kinda meh speically when trying to do chaos trials good luck, but if your not stinky like me for casual play I think its fine.

I got so angry at the story ending I stopped playing for a week but then went ahhh I like the gameplay so I went back to it.

The music and Art is honestly some of the best and I really appreciate it.

Games like a 8/10. Would rate higher but I literally cannot stand the ending teehee.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that late-game resource farming and quest progression require an extensive amount of grinding.

citations.review_text:
i hate to write negative review here and actually i liked my first 40 hours or so, but in the end you have to grind a lot: 
- the dialogs (the necessary you need to progress the quest could pop up not for ages, you can do 20 runs just for that and nothing)
- the weapon upgrades (the game push you to use weapon you hate and go specific boss, but then what, you can just die and that it, no challenge just grind. The game has the same reward whatever vows you have)
- the items to actually win the game (the real ending) > you need crazy amount of run just for farm items
so the game actually short, but they make it longer artificially
my gameplay in hades 1 was like you jump in - look real ending, add some challenge by vows. simple.
here my gameplay: farm stupid items, and dialogs (the most annoying), in the moment i finish the game i dont really wanna to challenge anything (max vows or at least to look how many you can get)

[b] the resume [/b]: if you plan to just "kill" both sides 1 times - this is awesome game
if you plan to open everything - this is grind game - if you dislike that  in such games - you probably should skip

PS forgot to mention final quest (spoilers ahead): [spoiler] you do not need to win, you need to die, the game is not encourage yours wins at all. [/spoiler]
Fun game loop. A little bit more forced-grind than Hades 1 to get necessary crafting materials, but keeps things interesting.

A near perfect sequel to the original Hades. Introduces a lot of new ideas and ways to play. Like the first Hades, bosses are tough - but fair. I really enjoyed this one. Some of the late game resource collection got a bit grindy, but outside of that every run and every challenge (except for the Great Chaos Below), was a blast.

English Version (french below) : 

Just take what was good in the first game and expend upon it. More bosses, multiples routes, more weapons, more music, more boons. 
Most weapons feel good to use, and each weapon has at least one aspect that feels very good, even if it's not always the default one (but then again, weapon feel is subjective).
And I mean, the game always feels hard without being unfair, still as tense and rewarding as the first one. 

However, it can get annoying if you don't get some of the random events considering how many there are (if you want do to the platinum at least). Other than that, I don't have a lot of flaws that come to mind right now.

The ending was changed significantly, and I honestly think it now fits a lot more with the spirit of the game and puts Melinoe as the central character she was meant to be.

If you liked the first one, go ahead and play it, you won't be disappointed.




Version Française : 

Prenez ce qui était bien dans le premier et améliorez le. Plus de boss, des routes multiples, plus d'armes, de musiques, de bénédictions...
La grande plupart des armes ont un bon feeling, et chaque arme a au moins un aspect qui vous plaira, même si ce n'est pas forcément celui de base (mais bon, c'est subjectif).
Et puis, le jeu est toujours dur sans être injuste, toujours aussi tendu et agréable que le premier jeu.

Par contre, ça peut devenir frustrant si vous n'arrivez pas à trigger certains des évènements aléatoires entre chaque partie (surtout si vous cherchez a avoir le platinum). A part ça, il n'y a pas particulièrement de défaut qui me viennent maintenant.

La fin a été changée significativement, et je trouve qu'elle correspond bien plus à l'esprit du jeu et elle met Melinoe plus comme le personnage central qu'elle était censée être.

Si vous avez aimé le premier, allez-y, vous ne serez pas déçu
solid gameplay, horrible rng that prevent the progress of story / quests (worst I've seen) to the point that it ruins the fun if you want to complete everything and learn all the stories.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the visual art style, character design, and soundtrack are exceptionally high quality.

citations.review_text:
One of my all-time favourite games. The combat is fast-paced and fun. The characters are incredibly well voice-acted and are such a joy to listen to. The gameplay and story are top tier. There were so many moments where I stopped and just listened to the soundtrack and took it all in. This game will stick with me for a long time.

Death to Chronos.

Hades 2 is without doubt one of the best ARPG's made to date. If it had a coop I would lose my beeeeeeeans. All systems are improved from the previous entry. The lore is amazing and the visual style is peak Super Giant. The OST is remarkable 10/10 buy it, love it, rub it all over.

Absolutely top tier game. Hades 2 has been a rollercoaster experience for me and I have loved every second of it. The writing, art style, and gameplay are all phenomenal. I've been blown away by the beauty of this game and it's striking visuals that add so much depth to the mythological experience. Often are the days I get sucked into the game, and play for hours on end in hopes to further deepen the story or unlock new weapons and their special forms. The game is fantastic for experienced or beginner players, as you can use the testament of night to increase the difficulty by insane levels. Supergiant games, Thank you so much for this beautiful game. 10/10.
My favorite game of all time. There is too much to say about it, it only was a genre from I thought I would not like. If that doesn't speak volume, the art style and music should blow your mind

Good game, sadly completed it all before they added more dialouge and I was too lazy to re do stuff.

I think out of the two games the first one has a better feel for fighting solely based on the fact U speed around with dodgeing around more so my ADHD brain feels like im doing more.

Some of the wepons and accesories are just kinda meh speically when trying to do chaos trials good luck, but if your not stinky like me for casual play I think its fine.

I got so angry at the story ending I stopped playing for a week but then went ahhh I like the gameplay so I went back to it.

The music and Art is honestly some of the best and I really appreciate it.

Games like a 8/10. Would rate higher but I literally cannot stand the ending teehee.
